title: Problem and Bayesian network
summary: The physical system and the model that describes it.

steps.title: Earthquake inspection prioritisation
steps.text: Earthquake inspection prioritisation for the Eastern Massachusetts highway benchmark network. Start with no observations or results.

steps.title: The inspection decision
steps.text: After an earthquake, which bridge inspections would help restore access to the airports?

steps.title: Shaking · SA(1.0)
steps.text: Blue nodes describe uncertain shaking at each bridge.

steps.title: Station readings · SAObs(1.0)
steps.text: Orange nodes model station readings, including measurement uncertainty.

steps.title: Bridge damage · DamageState
steps.text: Green nodes translate shaking into probabilities of bridge damage.

steps.title: Road availability · EdgeOpen
steps.text: Yellow nodes describe whether each road is open or closed.

steps.title: Community access · SystemState
steps.text: Pink nodes show whether communities can reach an airport within the allowed extra travel time.

title: Clique tree and inference
summary: Follow every message direction through the inference circuit.

steps.title: Four connections · eight directions
steps.text: Four connection types carry eight message directions, repeated across bridges and towns.

steps.title: 1 / 8 · Measurement → bridge
steps.text: A station reading sends a likelihood over the bridge's shaking.

steps.title: 2 / 8 · Bridge → hub
steps.text: Each bridge combines the likelihood with damage and road-state information.

steps.title: 3 / 8 · Hub → root
steps.text: The hub combines local messages and sends them to the root.

steps.title: 4 / 8 · Access → root
steps.text: Observed access constrains possible combinations of road states.

steps.title: Root update · certificate MCMC
steps.text: With access evidence, certificate MCMC updates road states. Otherwise, they are drawn directly.

steps.title: 5 / 8 · Root → hub
steps.text: Road samples return to the hub, where elliptical slice sampling updates shaking.

steps.title: 6 / 8 · Hub → bridge
steps.text: Shaking and road samples return to each bridge, updating its damage state.

steps.title: 7 / 8 · Bridge → measurement
steps.text: Shaking samples return to generate unobserved station readings.

steps.title: 8 / 8 · Root → access
steps.text: Road samples return to system cliques, which evaluate airport access.

title: Decision task and evidence
summary: Select an inspection task and add a station observation.

steps.title: Start a fresh session
steps.text: Start with a fresh session, then run the baseline.

steps.title: Choose the decision task
steps.text: Choose bridge inspection to prioritise people's access to key destinations.

steps.title: Calculating priorities
steps.text: The initial priorities are calculated. Waiting time is shortened here.

steps.title: A task that stays active
steps.text: The active task updates its priorities as new observations arrive.

steps.title: Enter an observation
steps.text: For this example, enter a ground-motion reading of zero point zero five g at bridge e seventy-three.

steps.title: Build the evidence base
steps.text: Add the observation to update the model and the inspection priorities.

steps.title: Updating with evidence
steps.text: The observation is being incorporated. Waiting time is shortened here.

steps.title: Evidence is now recorded
steps.text: The reading is now in the evidence base. Next, check the results in Roadmap and the Bayesian network.

title: Read the results
summary: Compare inspection priorities and BN distributions.

steps.title: Newest analysis first
steps.text: Roadmap shows the newest analysis first.

steps.title: Compare the priorities
steps.text: Grey is the previous round. Blue shows the updated inspection priorities.

steps.title: Read the leading candidate
steps.text: Bridge E one twenty-five still ranks first, at about fifty-one people whose access could be restored.

steps.title: Actual computation time
steps.text: Each milestone keeps its actual computation time.

steps.title: Inspect a BN variable
steps.text: In the Bayesian network, click the shaking node for bridge E seventy-three.

steps.title: See how uncertainty changes
steps.text: The reading narrows the shaking distribution. Its median shifts from point one two one to point zero five one g.

title: Customise your system
summary: Edit network.json, validate it and run a fresh analysis.

steps.title: Describe your system
steps.text: Your system is described in network dot json, with nodes, roads and bridges.

steps.title: Choose an attribute to change
steps.text: Find the road you want to change.

steps.title: Edit the data and save
steps.text: Here, change road E seventy-three's assumed speed from sixty to forty kilometres per hour, then save.

steps.title: Validate the inputs
steps.text: Run python minus m src check to validate the data and model.

steps.title: Reload the changed network
steps.text: Restart the server, then begin a new session to load the changed network.

steps.title: Compute the new baseline
steps.text: The actual inference wait is shortened here.

steps.title: Analyse your edited system
steps.text: The new baseline uses your edited data. Network dot json defines system data; the assembly defines model choices.
